_operation: calendar.events.list (a query with a disallowed restriction on an incremental sync)
_why: P5-005 requires recorded wire fixtures. This is NOT a recorded provider response. It reproduces the Calendar errors page's own 400 Bad Request body, whose documented example reason is `timeRangeEmpty`.
_the_point_of_this_fixture: A 400 ON AN INCREMENTAL SYNC IS NOT A STALE CURSOR, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE WHOLE REASON THE 410 EXISTS. The sync guide says the response code for list queries "containing disallowed restrictions is 400", while a 410 means the sync token is invalid. The remedies are opposites: 400 is the CALLER's mistake -- the same query must not be repeated -- and 410 is a full wipe. A connector that resynced on any incremental-sync failure would discard a working store because it sent a bad filter; one that refused on 410 would loop forever on a dead token.
_why_the_reason_matters: The page states plainly: "Because this is a permanent error, do not retry. Read the error message instead and change your request accordingly." So this fixture also pins that the connector must not treat a 400 as retryable -- and, separately, that it must not resync.
_the_two_documented_400_reasons: timeRangeEmpty: 'The specified time range is empty.' (locationType: parameter, location: timeMax) -- the example this fixture reproduces
the page's prose also covers a missing required field, an invalid value, and an invalid field combination, all with the same remedy
_sanitized: No real message text, request id, address, or calendar id appears here.
